chitchat: Two hundred and eleven. It was two hundred and nineteen in the spring.
Don't touch a rack. Touch me if you want to know what cold is.
Every one of these is somebody who hasn't decided yet.
It takes nine years to make what's in this room.
description:
A small still woman standing with both palms flat on a rack of flasks. She has been doing that for a while.

Her hands run about twenty degrees under yours. It isn't a trick and it isn't comfortable to shake, and it's the entire reason she has the most important job in the Thornwarren: two hundred and eleven flasks and no machine anywhere in the region that could hold them at temperature, and one woman who can.

She looks up when you come in and doesn't stop what she's doing.

bye.text:
"Right."

And they go back to it, which out here is the whole of a goodbye.

gaps.text:
She doesn't look at the log.

"Eighty-one, eighty-two, ninety-four, one-eleven, one-thirty."

A pause.

"Eighty-one was Renna Ford. Eighty-two was her brother, four days later, because he wouldn't let her do it on her own." She lays her hands flat on the rack again. "Every gap is a person and I know all of them and that's on purpose. Somebody has to."

"Tallow keeps the tally on her wall so the town can see the numbers. I keep this one so somebody keeps the names."

root.first: "Shut the door." Then, after she has heard it shut: "Thank you. Most people leave it."

options.label: There are gaps in the numbering.

text_by_relation.close: She takes her hands off the rack when you come in, which costs her, and doesn't mention it.
text_by_relation.familiar: "Hold this a moment," and she puts a flask in your hand, which is a thing she doesn't do.
text_by_relation.known: "You shut it." Approval, from her, is enormous. "Good."

stock.text:
"The Pool, settled."

She turns one in its felt so the label faces out.

"You can't use it as it comes. Straight out of the water it'll kill you nine times in ten and the tenth isn't worth having. It has to stand. Nine years, dark and cold, and then Tallow tests it and then it goes in a rack and waits for somebody."

She puts it back.

"There's no more. Not anywhere. The Pool gives what it gives and it isn't much and this is all of it, so when you hear somebody in the Basin say we hand it out, you'll know exactly how much they know."
